description: Work out which tables and columns of a data model its dashboards need, ready to build a perspective from.

datamodel.description: The data model, as an ID or title.

detailed.description: Include the per-dashboard, per-column, per-dependency and per-issue detail. Default ``False`` returns the summary view only.

examples.user_query: Analyze all dashboards for the 'Sales Data Model' and include detailed results for dependencies and issues.
examples.notes: This call analyzes the 'Sales Data Model' to determine which tables and columns are required for its dashboards, providing detailed insights into dependencies and issues. Use this when you need a comprehensive breakdown of dashboard requirements.

examples.user_query: Which tables and columns are needed for the 'Marketing Analytics' data model?
examples.notes: This call provides a summary of the tables and columns required for dashboards using the 'Marketing Analytics' data model. Use this for a high-level overview without detailed dependency information.

examples.user_query: Show me the perspective requirements for the data model 'Customer Insights' with detailed analysis.
examples.notes: This call analyzes the 'Customer Insights' data model and provides detailed perspective requirements, including per-dashboard and per-column details. Use this when building or refining perspectives for dashboards tied to this model.

description: Create a perspective over a data model, keeping only the named tables and columns.

datamodel.description: The root data model, as an ID or title.

name.description: Name for the new perspective. Must not already exist on that model.

tables.description: Tables to keep. Each entry is ``{"table": name, "columns": [names] | "all"}``, or a bare table name meaning all of its columns. Tables not listed are excluded.

description.description: Description shown in Sisense. Default empty.

ai_context.description: Free-text context for the AI assistant, stored on the perspective as ``aiContext``.

examples.user_query: Create a perspective named 'Sales Overview' on the 'Global Sales' data model, keeping only the 'Orders' table with all columns and the 'Customers' table with the 'Name' and 'Region' columns.
examples.notes: This creates a perspective named 'Sales Overview' that includes all columns from the 'Orders' table and only the 'Name' and 'Region' columns from the 'Customers' table. Use this to create a focused view of the data model.

examples.user_query: Can you create a perspective called 'Marketing Insights' for the 'Campaign Analytics' model, keeping only the 'Campaigns' table with all columns?
examples.notes: This creates a perspective named 'Marketing Insights' that includes all columns from the 'Campaigns' table. Useful for isolating campaign-related data.

examples.user_query: I need a perspective named 'Finance Summary' on the 'Corporate Finance' model, keeping the 'Transactions' table with all columns and the 'Accounts' table with only the 'Account Name' column. Add a description saying 'Summary of financial data for reporting.'

arguments.name: Finance Summary
arguments.description: Summary of financial data for reporting.

examples.notes: This creates a perspective named 'Finance Summary' with a description. It includes all columns from the 'Transactions' table and only the 'Account Name' column from the 'Accounts' table. Ideal for financial reporting purposes.

description: Delete a perspective by name or ID.

datamodel.description: Root data model (ID or title) to disambiguate a name that exists on several models.

examples.user_query: Delete the perspective named 'Sales Overview' from the data model titled 'Global Sales'.
examples.notes: This call deletes the 'Sales Overview' perspective from the 'Global Sales' data model. Use this when you need to remove a specific perspective and the data model title is required to disambiguate.

examples.user_query: How can I remove the perspective with ID 'persp_12345'?
examples.notes: This call deletes the perspective with the specified ID. Use this when the perspective ID is known and there is no ambiguity about the associated data model.

examples.user_query: Delete the perspective named 'Regional Insights' from the data model with ID 'model_67890'.
examples.notes: This call deletes the 'Regional Insights' perspective from the data model identified by 'model_67890'. Use this when the perspective name exists on multiple models and the data model ID is needed for clarification.

description: Retrieve perspectives — all of them, those of one data model, or specific ones by name or ID.

perspectives.description: One perspective reference or a list of them, each a name (case-insensitive) or an ``oid``. ``None`` returns all.

datamodel.description: Root data model to restrict to, as an ID or title.

include_default.description: Include the auto-generated ``Default`` perspectives when listing. Default ``False``.

examples.user_query: Retrieve all perspectives for the 'Sales Data' data model, including the default ones.
examples.notes: This call retrieves all perspectives associated with the 'Sales Data' data model, including the auto-generated 'Default' perspective.

examples.user_query: What perspectives exist for the 'Marketing Analytics' data model?
examples.notes: This call lists all perspectives for the 'Marketing Analytics' data model, excluding the default perspective unless explicitly requested.

examples.user_query: Find the perspectives named 'Executive View' and 'Regional Breakdown'.
examples.notes: This call retrieves the perspectives named 'Executive View' and 'Regional Breakdown' across all data models.
